title: Current and Landfall
premise: Desert ranger Casper Nakamura, a former cartographer's apprentice who fled the fallen Republic of Veyra three years ago, pulls a seal-stamped chest from the river and finds inside a map to the Republic's hidden treasury—and his own name on the manifest. Hunted by a corrupt Veyran colonel who wants the treasury to buy himself a new nation, Casper must cross the Serpent Range before snowfall closes the passes, gathering an unlikely crew: the thief he was chasing, a defected soldier, and an orphaned stonemason's daughter. At the pass, Casper learns the treasury is a lie concealing the Republic's last census rolls—proof that could restore legitimacy to survivors the colonel wants erased. Casper chooses to burn the colonel's claim and scatter the rolls to the people they name, finding that belonging was something he built on the road, not something he lost.
about_author: B. M. Nakamura is the pen name of a former trail-crew foreman who spent a decade mapping washes and ghost towns across the high desert before turning to fiction. Their work blends granular landscape detail with stories about people who measure their lives in distances rather than years.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Establishes his solitary routine tracking a thief named Wren Sallow across the flats, and his habit of counting days in distance. He catches Wren's trail at a dead spring. Beat: loneliness mistaken for peace.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. A flash flood recedes, exposing a chest stamped with Veyra's seal. Inside: a manifest listing names—including his. He realizes someone knows he survived the Republic's fall. Beat: dread breaking through routine.

chapters.title: The Thief Who Waited
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren reveals she was hired to steal the chest and deliver it to a colonel named Ashgrave; she kept it instead when she read the names. Uneasy alliance forms. Beat: wary mutual recognition of survivors.

chapters.title: Ashgrave's Ledger
chapters.summary: Colonel Ashgrave's POV. He interrogates a captured courier, revealing he intends to use the chest's contents to buy mercenary legitimacy for a resurrected Veyra under his rule. Beat: cold ambition; the antagonist's logic made seductive.

chapters.title: Three Days to the Range
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper and Wren ride for the Serpent Range ahead of early snows, pursued by Ashgrave's outriders. Casper teaches Wren desert craft; she teaches him to sleep in shifts again. Beat: trust as a practical skill.

chapters.title: The Stonemason's Daughter
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In a dying way-station town they rescue Ila, twelve, whose father was killed for repairing a Veyran milestone. Ila refuses to be left behind. Beat: found family begins as inconvenience, then necessity.

chapters.title: Salt and Ash
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Flashback woven into present: the night Casper fled Veyra's purge, abandoning his mentor the cartographer. He admits to Wren why his name was on the manifest—he drew the original treasury map. Beat: guilt surfaced.

chapters.title: Outriders at the Ford
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Ashgrave's men corner them at a river ford; a defected soldier, Sergeant Bek Odumane, turns her rifle on her own unit to save the group. She joins them. Beat: defection as the first act of a new loyalty.

chapters.title: The Map That Lies
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Studying his own old map, Casper realizes the treasury coordinates are wrong—deliberately. The chest is bait; the real cargo is elsewhere. Beat: the trap inverts; they must decide whether to run or mislead.

chapters.title: Ashgrave's Offer
chapters.summary: Ashgrave's POV. He captures a messenger and sends terms to Casper: the map for amnesty, a commission, a home. Casper reads it aloud to the group. Beat: temptation framed as belonging—the corrupt version of what they're building.

chapters.title: Ila's Milestone
chapters.summary: Ila's POV (first child's-eye chapter). Ila secretly repairs a shattered milestone with Veyra's seal, insisting the Republic's dead deserve their names kept. The adults argue, then help her. Beat: memory as inheritance, not burden.

chapters.title: First Snow on the Serpent
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. They reach the foothills as snow begins; the low pass is already closed. Only the high traverse remains, three days' climb. Bek reveals Ashgrave has bribed the pass wardens. Beat: the door narrowing.

chapters.title: The Warden's Price
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. They confront Warden Tessaly, an old friend of Casper's mentor, who demands a price: the truth of what happened to the cartographer. Casper confesses he ran instead of fighting. Tessaly opens the pass. Beat: confession as toll.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. A storm traps them in a cave; supplies dwindle. Bek's frostbite worsens. Ila tells stories to keep everyone awake. Beat: vulnerability binding the group into family.

chapters.title: What Bek Carried
chapters.summary: Bek's POV. Recovering, Bek reveals she served under Ashgrave at the purge and recognizes the census rolls' significance—the treasury was always a cover for the lists of survivors. Beat: the stakes reframe from gold to people.

chapters.title: The False Summit
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. They reach the traverse's midpoint and find Ashgrave's vanguard already dug in, waiting—Tessaly sold the timing. Ambush kills two of Bek's old comrades who defected with her. Beat: betrayal; the cost of the climb.

chapters.title: Casper's Coordinates
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper devises a plan: feed Ashgrave false coordinates to the 'treasury'—a dead mine—while the group splits to reach the true cache of census rolls. Wren volunteers to play the traitor. Beat: resolve forged; everyone has a role.

chapters.title: Wren's Bargain
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren delivers the false map to Ashgrave, who sees through it halfway and takes her prisoner, marching her to the mine as insurance. She stalls, lies, survives on nerve. Beat: courage under a blade.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Climax, Casper's POV. At the mine, Ashgrave forces the confrontation; Casper offers himself in exchange for Wren and the rolls. Ashgrave's mercenaries, shown the rolls bearing their own families' names, refuse to fire. Beat: power corrupts; belonging outvotes it.

chapters.title: The Burning Manifest
chapters.summary: Ashgrave's POV, final time. Beaten, Ashgrave burns the chest rather than surrender it, destroying his claim to resurrect Veyra. He walks into the snow alone. Beat: the emptiness of stolen legitimacy.

chapters.title: Scattering the Names
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The group copies and distributes the census rolls to survivor settlements along the river, giving the displaced their documented past. Casper keeps one page: his mentor's name. Beat: restitution, grief honored.

chapters.title: A Life Measured in People
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, epilogue. Spring. Casper, Wren, Bek, and Ila establish a way-station at the ford, a home for those the rolls named. He stops counting miles. Beat: belonging chosen, not inherited; the arc closed.
